answer: A transitive credit protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by routing transactions across an interlocking reef of peer-vetted trust edges. Path-based routing maintains crystal clarity over flow capacity by enforcing bounded bilateral limits. An attacker must lock scarce liquid capital per identity to secure usable credit, preventing them from hiding behind an umber haze of forged nodes. However, this severely constrains routing liquidity and blocks honest, unsponsored newcomers.
